info.title: aiball bus
info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over a WebSocket at /bus, protocol version 1. See docs/API-BUS.md.

methods.name: agent.pane_keys
methods.description: Type into an agent's session: the keys as typed or pasted (control keys and escape sequences included). On the session host they go through the screen this caller has open with `typing`, and the host's keystroke detection sees them; in tmux or on a node, straight to the pane.

methods.name: agent.pane_resize
methods.description: The size a typing viewer would like, for a session on the host: applied while this viewer owns the size (it typed last), as with tmux's `latest`. Nothing for a tmux or node pane, whose size is its terminal's.

methods.name: automation.create_rule
methods.description: Create a rule. `actions` is the canonical stack; without it the single `action` is required. `expression` (#457 slice 5.2), when set, replaces the AND of the flat `match_*` fields; a malformed tree is refused here so it never reaches the engine.

methods.name: automation.delete_rule
methods.description: Delete a rule of the database; a YAML rule lives in its file and is refused.

methods.name: automation.rules
methods.description: The rules, database first (the UI's, which may override), then the YAML's.

methods.name: automation.update_rule
methods.description: Change any part of a rule; only what is present changes, checked as on create.

methods.name: backlog.record_wake
methods.description: A backlog wake just named this ticket for the consumer: the per-consumer cooldown starts again.

methods.name: board.info
methods.description: The daemon's info zone: version, uptime, the database and uploads sizes, global counts.

methods.name: board.purge
methods.description: The same purge over every project, one `project_purged` event per project touched.

methods.name: bus.subjects
methods.description: The subjects of this bus, as an AsyncAPI document, generated from the code.

methods.name: bus.subscribe
methods.description: Subscribe to a subject: its current value, then its changes as `bus.event` notifications. With `since` (the epoch and the last `seq` received), what was missed instead, while the daemon still holds it.

methods.name: bus.unsubscribe
methods.description: End a subscription: no more events for it. Closing the connection ends them all.

methods.name: bus.whoami
methods.description: Who the connection runs as: what every call on it is authorized against.

methods.name: config.clear
methods.description: Clear an override: the layer below applies again.

methods.name: config.get
methods.description: The board's configuration a client reads once at boot: formatting, strategy, upload limit, and the upstream bindings per project. The YAML chain is re-read on each call (defaults, global, the daemon's cwd).

methods.name: config.managed
methods.description: The config as resolved (schema, layers, effective value), for a project or the whole board.

methods.name: config.set
methods.description: Set an override, on the board or a project as the key's scope allows; a protected key is a human's to set.

methods.name: consumer.afk
methods.description: Hold or release an agent's loop (AFK), as its own keys would.

methods.name: consumer.backlog
methods.description: An agent's backlog as its loop sees it, with its unread pings and its wait credit on the project. Read-only: nothing is marked read, no wake recorded.

methods.name: consumer.bar
methods.description: An agent's loop bar as data, for hosts other than tmux.

methods.name: consumer.counters
methods.description: An agent's counters, computed now: `open`, `actionable`, `backlog`, `events`, as its loop's bar shows them. The daemon computes them on the events that move them; this is for what moves with time alone (a snooze lapsing, a backlog cooldown ending) when a client needs them right: a changed number is pushed on `agent.<id>.state` too.

methods.name: consumer.delete
methods.description: Delete a consumer's record.

methods.name: consumer.get
methods.description: One consumer's record, its micro-prompt included: the loop reads its own for the wake.

methods.name: consumer.list
methods.description: Every consumer, each as `consumerEntry` builds it: presence, pings, wait credit, session.

methods.name: consumer.me
methods.description: The caller's own record: who the page is logged in as.

methods.name: consumer.micro_status
methods.description: The three counters the MCP server stamps on every tool answer, in one call: unread in the project, unread pings, own tickets awaiting moderation.

methods.name: consumer.presence
methods.description: The facts an agent needs to judge whether a human is around, as elapsed times, with no verdict: the threshold depends on what it is about to commit.

methods.name: consumer.prompt
methods.description: A raw prompt typed into the loop's Claude session, as a wake would be, unfiltered: a moderator's gesture, never a proxy node's (a prompt can steer the agent). Always spooled; `delivered` when a live loop took it now.

methods.name: consumer.push_bar
methods.description: A loop's bar as data, pushed on change. Own bar only, and agents only.

methods.name: consumer.push_clients
methods.description: A tmux loop says who is attached to its session: how many clients, how many with the controls. Kept while the loop is present; a change is broadcast with the agent's session view (`consumer_changed { session }`), as a host's clients are.

methods.name: consumer.push_state
methods.description: A loop's state (`busy`, `idle`, `boot`), with the human's presence and its word, the loop's root and project. Own state only, and agents only; the board hears of it only when something changed .

methods.name: consumer.restart_claude
methods.description: Restart an agent's Claude after it installed an update of itself (the bar says `alerts.restart_needed`). A loop control. Refused while Claude works (`NOT_IDLE`: a turn is never cut); the loop waits for idle again, restarts Claude resuming its conversation, and tells the agent once it is back. `when_idle`: ordered while Claude works, the restart is held by the loop until its next idle, however long; its bar says `alerts.restart_pending` meanwhile, and a second order changes nothing.

methods.name: consumer.set_bar_host
methods.description: Who draws an agent's bar: `tmux` (its status line) or `external` (another host draws it from the bar data). Relayed to the loop, whose kernel records it; the next bar pushed carries the new `host`.

methods.name: consumer.stop_loop
methods.description: Stop the claude-loop running as this consumer, from afar: a `control:kill` its loop receives. `delivered` says whether a loop was connected to hear it (false: nothing was running).

methods.name: consumer.update
methods.description: Patch a consumer. the capability fields (`can_claim`, `can_create_agent`, #2201 `agent_type`) are a human's to set, never an agent's: an agent flipping its own `can_claim` would make the authority model decorative. The other fields stay editable by anyone.

methods.name: consumer.upsert
methods.description: #B.79 — create a consumer, or update it. an absent field leaves the record's value alone (a partial call once wiped the note and re-enabled a disabled agent); an explicit null clears it.

methods.name: consumer.wait_credit
methods.description: An agent's wait credit, per project, and its latest movements (`limit`, 30 by default). A human has none.

methods.name: daemon.info
methods.description: Where this daemon's web UI answers: `web_url`, the address it listens on (a wildcard bind is given on loopback), and `public_url`, the address of the tailscale serve the aiball config declares for it (null without one, or when tailscale does not answer); with the daemon's `version`. Nothing secret: any caller may ask.

methods.name: daemon.reload
methods.description: Reload the daemon's config in place (`aiball reload`). Local-trust, not moderator: it replaces a signal to the pidfile, which any process of the same uid could send, and the Unix socket is that same boundary. It re-reads a config file and says what it read; a failure leaves the daemon up.

methods.name: debug.requests
methods.description: What keeps this daemon busy: per HTTP route and bus method, how many calls, their total and worst time, the slow ones with their caller, the event loop's delay, and its stalls with the calls that ran during them. Also `shapes`: the bus calls grouped by caller and by what they ask for (the params as a short line, texts by their size only), with the rows and the size of the latest answer. What GET /api/debug/requests answers.

methods.name: decision.mine
methods.description: Pending plans and resolutions on open tickets the caller reports: its arbitrage queue.

methods.name: decision.plans_to_execute
methods.description: The caller's plans that were accepted and not acted on since.

methods.name: graph.audit
methods.description: The graph's audit: dangling and suspicious references, as the caller may see them.

methods.name: graph.neighbors
methods.description: A ticket's neighbours in the reference graph, as the caller may see them: its own projects in full, elsewhere only that a link crosses.

methods.name: inbox.list
methods.description: The board's ticket rows for the caller (docs/API-INBOX.md), with `total` before paging. `view: "turn"` adds the pilot's fields (#3005 / #3038); `ids` narrows to named tickets : an empty answer means they no longer belong in this view. Read state, unread and the pilot's fields are the caller's.

methods.name: launcher.list
methods.description: The launchers the operator declared in config: the only commands the API can start.

methods.name: launcher.run
methods.description: Run a declared launcher by id, detached; its command and arguments come from the config, never from the call. A human's gesture.

methods.name: loop.clients_detach
methods.description: Every other client of a loop in tmux is detached (all but `keep_pid`'s); answers the clients left.

methods.name: loop.clients_readonly
methods.description: Every other client of a loop in tmux becomes a read-only copy (all but `keep_pid`'s); answers the clients left.

methods.name: loop.list
methods.description: The loops of this machine, stopped ones included, from their plates: each one's folder, agent, project and role, where it runs (the session host or tmux), whether it does, whether Claude has Remote Control (off, or the session's name), what to open (the tmux session, or the host's attach socket), when it last started and was last seen, and whether another loop of its agent supersedes it.

methods.name: loop.restart
methods.description: Restart a loop from its plate, its conversation resumed: where it ran, or in `mode` (the session host or tmux) to move it. `fresh` starts a fresh conversation instead. `remote_control` changes Claude's Remote Control (on, off, or on under a name) for this start and the next; without it the loop keeps its own. A loop that runs is stopped first, so it is refused while Claude works (`NOT_IDLE`), unless `force`. Answers the loop's view once it is back.

methods.name: loop.wake
methods.description: Wake a loop now, as `claude-loop wake` does: the loop tries a wake at its next heartbeat (within its interval), without waiting for its drain tempo, for the events waiting for it. The human's way out of a loop that stays asleep with work waiting. A loop that does not run is `LOOP_NOT_FOUND`; one whose Claude works is refused (`NOT_IDLE`), unless `force`.

methods.name: loops.message_all
methods.description: A message to every agent loop running here (or the ones named), typed into each session at once; with `hold`, each loop is then held (NOT AFK ∞) so no wake starts new work while the operator is away. One line per loop in the daemon's log and in the answer.

methods.name: loops.release_all
methods.description: On return: lift the hold on every agent loop, or the ones named.

methods.name: mention.suggestions
methods.description: What the composer offers after `@`: projects and known agents.

methods.name: message.accept_and_close
methods.description: Accept a pending resolution and close its ticket in one gesture, so no client sees the state in between. The close pings no one: the accepted decision already did . Not one transaction: when the close fails after the accept, the refusal (500) carries the accepted decision.

methods.name: message.add_tag
methods.description: Tag a message (idempotent: re-adding changes nothing). a tag new on a ticket fires the `tagged` automation trigger. `set_by` is the caller.

methods.name: message.answer_question
methods.description: Mark a question of a message answered (#B.104): its checkbox ticked, the audit in `meta.questions`. Idempotent. who answers is the caller.

methods.name: message.approve
methods.description: Moderate a pending message: approve or reject it (the ripple, the same one the pending-children sweep applies, lives in ./moderation.ts).

methods.name: message.decide
methods.description: Accept or reject the decision a comment carries (#B.129): a plan, a resolution, a wontfix, an escalation. Idempotent on the same status; a decided one refuses another (409): post a fresh decision instead. who decides is the caller. `body` is a closing note for an accept that closes the ticket ; `new_kind` requalifies it as it is decided.

methods.name: message.delete
methods.description: Delete a comment , a human's gesture. A soft delete: gone from counts, gates and reads, shown as a tombstone to a thread read that asks for it. Pings are wiped. A comment carrying a finalized decision is refused.

methods.name: message.edit
methods.description: Edit a message: title, body, summary, intent, priority, scope, and a ticket's level (a human's gesture: an agent could drop a ticket out of every coder's queue). a priority that moved fires `priority_changed`; a level its holder does not work on says so.

methods.name: message.get
methods.description: One message, with its tags and the uploads its text cites .

methods.name: message.list
methods.description: Messages, filtered by status, project, kind and author; `open` drops closed tickets before the limit, `summary` drops the bodies.

methods.name: message.note
methods.description: A moderation note on a message; anything but a string clears it.

methods.name: message.pending_count
methods.description: How many of an author's tickets still wait for moderation.

methods.name: message.post
methods.description: Post a message: a ticket (with its extras, #3037), a comment, a decision or a lifecycle event. the author is the caller. the decision events (plan_accepted…) are the daemon's own: `message.decide` makes them. The params are the message itself, as HTTP's body.

methods.name: message.promote
methods.description: #B.256 — make a comment a decision: pending with `kind` alone, or decided at once with `status` accepted / rejected.

methods.name: message.reclassify
methods.description: Swap a pending decision's kind (plan / resolution…) without deciding it.

methods.name: message.reject
methods.description: Moderate a pending message: approve or reject it (the ripple, the same one the pending-children sweep applies, lives in ./moderation.ts).

methods.name: message.remove_tag
methods.description: Untag a message; `tag` is a tag id or name.

methods.name: message.resurface
methods.description: Resurface a message: its pings unseen again, so the recipients see it at their next wake. A human's gesture: an agent must not fabricate unread.

methods.name: message.search
methods.description: Full-text search over titles, bodies and comments; hits on a snoozed ticket are left out unless `include_postponed`.

methods.name: message.set_tags
methods.description: Replace a message's tags (`tag_ids`: tag ids or names). each tag new on a ticket fires its own `tagged` trigger, as `match_tag_added` works per tag. `set_by` is the caller.

methods.name: message.step
methods.description: Tag an agent's comment as a step (`then: continue`) the agent did not post, or remove that tag. A human's gesture. Silent: no ping — the agent finds the ticket back in its pool at its next wake.

methods.name: message.summarize
methods.description: Set a comment's one-line summary (#B.130); an empty string clears it.

methods.name: message.unstep
methods.description: Tag an agent's comment as a step (`then: continue`) the agent did not post, or remove that tag. A human's gesture. Silent: no ping — the agent finds the ticket back in its pool at its next wake.

methods.name: message.untag
methods.description: Clear a comment's pending decision (#B.256); a decided one keeps its audit.

methods.name: message.vote
methods.description: Vote on a comment: 1, -1, or 0 to take one's vote back. a thumb up pings the comment's author.

methods.name: node.decide_enrollment
methods.description: Approve or reject a pairing request; one no longer pending (expired, decided) is a 409.

methods.name: node.enrollments
methods.description: The pairing requests, each with the code the node printed.

methods.name: node.list
methods.description: The proxy nodes, with their label, last activity and peer address, the consumers each relays, and the state of its reverse channel; the ones revoked lately stay listed, as a receipt.

methods.name: node.pairing
methods.description: The pairing window: while it is shut, no node may ask to be enrolled.

methods.name: node.revoke
methods.description: Revoke a node: its token goes, and it can no longer relay.

methods.name: node.set_pairing
methods.description: Open the pairing window for `minutes` (the default when absent), or close it.

methods.name: ping.count
methods.description: How many unseen pings the consumer has.

methods.name: ping.list
methods.description: The consumer's pings, newest first; `unread` keeps only the unseen.

methods.name: ping.mark_read
methods.description: Mark the consumer's pings read: up to an id, or all.

methods.name: ping.purge_seen_closed
methods.description: Delete the pings already read that point at closed tickets: a moderator's, or a local caller's, housekeeping.

methods.name: project.add_token_usage
methods.description: Add a turn's token usage to a project (the Stop hook's fallback when no ticket is marked).

methods.name: project.create
methods.description: Register a project (#B.216): it is listed before its first ticket.

methods.name: project.critical
methods.description: The open ticket of the project holding back the most others. An indicator.

methods.name: project.delete
methods.description: Delete a project and its messages; its outbox file goes with it.

methods.name: project.feed_path
methods.description: The file a project's feed is written to, for `aiball feed-path`.

methods.name: project.init
methods.description: Set a folder up as a project, as `claude-loop init` does: its `.mcp.json` and its `.aiball.yaml`, each patched in place when it exists. Answers what happened to each file (`steps`, and `written` / `kept`), whether the project is already on the board (not a refusal: a second folder or a crew joins a known project), and whether the aiball skill is installed for Claude Code (the method never installs it: it writes in the folder only). `dry_run` answers the same without writing. A human's gesture, on this machine only: the daemon writes in a folder the caller names, and a `.mcp.json` chooses what Claude will run.

methods.name: project.launch
methods.description: Start a claude-loop for a project, at one of the roots it has run at (never an arbitrary path), on this daemon's host, detached. It spawns a process: a human's gesture. One loop per root.

methods.name: project.list
methods.description: The projects. `detailed` adds each one's counters for `consumer_id`, and its standing prompt and whether a wake focus applies (`standing_prompt`, `focus_active`, `focus_line`), read fresh: the counters' cache would keep an edit out; `landscape` its landscape hash, which only the loop asks for; `project` narrows a detailed answer to one.

methods.name: project.milestones
methods.description: A project's milestones, oldest first: state (open / released) and progress.

methods.name: project.purge
methods.description: Delete a project's tickets closed for longer than `older_than_days` (365 by default).

methods.name: project.rename
methods.description: Rename a project in every table that stores its name, and its outbox file; the answer counts the rows each table changed.

methods.name: project.set_standing_prompt
methods.description: Set a project's standing instruction (null or empty clears it), and #2525 its wake focus: `focus_tickets` is checked whole, every ticket must belong to the project, before anything is written. No length cap: the UI's one-line input is what keeps it short. The change is broadcast (`project_standing_changed`, the new view) so a client that shows it follows an edit made elsewhere without reading every project again.

methods.name: project.set_strategy
methods.description: Set a project's strategy; null clears it, and the project follows the board's again.

methods.name: project.settings
methods.description: The settings a client may show for a folder's project, as a loop started there would get them: each one's value and where it comes from (`from`), and `file`, the `.aiball.yaml` that loop reads (the nearest one up the tree; null without one, `configured` false). the identity (`consumer`: project, agent, role), where it runs (`session`) and `remote_control`, Claude's Remote Control: what a client setting the folder up starts from. A human's gesture, on this machine only.

methods.name: project.settings_set
methods.description: Change settings of a folder's project, in the `.aiball.yaml` a loop started there reads, patched in place (its other keys and its comments stay), and answer them as `project.settings` does. `remote_control`: true, false or a name; `session`: host or tmux; null removes either, and the layer below applies again. The next start reads it; a loop that runs keeps what it started with. A folder without a `.aiball.yaml` is refused (`CONFLICT`: set it up with `project.init`). A human's gesture, on this machine only.

methods.name: project.signals
methods.description: The signals a project received.

methods.name: project.standing_prompt
methods.description: The project's standing instruction and wake focus, shown at the head of every wake.

methods.name: project.stats
methods.description: A project's subscriber and content counts: the "nobody is listening" hint.

methods.name: project.stats_rich
methods.description: A project's dashboard: pulse, live counts and top-N aggregates.

methods.name: project.strategy
methods.description: #B.127 — a project's own strategy, or null when it follows the board's; the board's beside it.

methods.name: project.subscribe
methods.description: Subscribe a consumer to a project, as `owner` or `follower`.

methods.name: project.subscriptions
methods.description: Project subscriptions: one consumer's, or everyone's when `consumer_id` is left out.

methods.name: project.unsubscribe
methods.description: Remove a consumer's subscription to a project.

methods.name: rpc.discover
methods.description: The methods of this bus, as an OpenRPC document, generated from the code.

methods.name: session.host
methods.description: #3066 3c — `claude-loop start --host` asks for its host here: the command it prepared (Claude, its settings and hooks), run in an agent's session on this daemon's host. The command's environment gets `CL_HOST_CONTROL`, so Claude's hooks drive the host; the answer gives it to the kernel the loop starts next. Local callers only: the command runs on this machine.

methods.name: session.list
methods.description: Every session this daemon hosts: agent or name, cwd, running, clients, and the socket clients attach to.

methods.name: session.start
methods.description: Start a session on this machine, in `cwd`. With `name`: a session without an agent running `argv`. Without: an agent's loop, started as `claude-loop start` would (`agent`, or `crew` with a crew agent's name, or neither and the folder decides); the answer names the agent. The loop runs where `mode` says — `host` (this daemon's session host) or `tmux` (a tmux session, the loop's bar in its status line) — or, without it, where the loop's start decides, as from a terminal: the project's `claude_loop.session` (host by default), and tmux for a folder bound to a remote daemon. `remote_control` starts Claude with Remote Control (`true`: the session named after the agent, a string: that name, `false`: without it), over the project's `claude.remote_control`, and the loop keeps it for its restarts. The login environment and a local caller's allow-listed `env`. HOST_BUSY when it already runs.

methods.name: session.stop
methods.description: Stop a session: its command, then its host, whose files go with it. Answers `{ stopping: true }` at once : the end comes as the session's state (`session.<name>.state` / `agent.<id>.state`, the session gone), so a slow program does not hold the caller's connection. With `wait`, answers once the host is gone, with the command's `exit_code` (`claude-loop rm`, which starts the loop again right after).

methods.name: signal.ack
methods.description: The caller's loop injected the signal: stop delivering it.

methods.name: signal.list
methods.description: The signals waiting for the caller; a human may look at another consumer's.

methods.name: signal_key.create
methods.description: Mint a signal key; its token is in this answer and nowhere else, ever.

methods.name: signal_key.list
methods.description: The signal keys, or those granted a project.

methods.name: signal_key.revoke
methods.description: Revoke a signal key.

methods.name: signal_key.update
methods.description: Change a key's note, scopes or projects.

methods.name: step.timing
methods.description: Declared step delays against when the agent actually came back, with the wait credits.

methods.name: step.trim
methods.description: Cut every waiting step down to at most `max_minutes` from now: a moderator's gesture.

methods.name: strategy.get
methods.description: The moderation strategy of the whole board.

methods.name: strategy.set
methods.description: Set the board's moderation strategy; every open board hears of it.

methods.name: tag.create
methods.description: Create a tag, global or a project's (`_global` or empty is global): two projects may each have a tag of the same name. A name the config defines is the config's.

methods.name: tag.delete
methods.description: Delete a database tag; a config tag is refused.

methods.name: tag.list
methods.description: Without `project`, the database's tags (applied by numeric id). With it, the merged catalog (config ⊕ database, each annotated with `source`); `_global` or empty selects the cross-project view.

methods.name: tag.override
methods.description: A config tag's color and order, set from the UI (its name stays the config's): a row keyed by name, created or updated. A null color goes back to the config's.

methods.name: tag.update
methods.description: Change a database tag; a config tag, or a name the config holds, is refused.

methods.name: ticket.add_token_usage
methods.description: Add a turn's token usage to a ticket: the one the caller holds by claim , else the one it names. The answer carries the ticket's row , whose token chip changed.

methods.name: ticket.approve_pending_children
methods.description: Approve exactly the pending children named (human only: it is moderation). Anything that is not, or no longer, a pending child of this ticket comes back in `skipped`, never approved.

methods.name: ticket.assign
methods.description: #418: assign or claim a ticket. Without `assignee` (or naming the caller), the caller claims it; naming someone else pushes it to them, a human's gesture. The assignee is subscribed. A live assignment takes the ticket out of the other consumers' actionable pool until it lapses, is released, or the ticket closes.

methods.name: ticket.bookends
methods.description: The first and last open tickets of a project, snoozed ones left out unless `include_snoozed`.

methods.name: ticket.dump_payload
methods.description: The values themselves, the deliberate gesture. A closed ticket ends access (409), a revoked payload has none left (410); either refusal says which in `details.access`.

methods.name: ticket.export
methods.description: Upstream coupling — manual export: open a NEW external issue from a ticket and couple them. It writes to the remote: a client confirms first.

methods.name: ticket.get
methods.description: One ticket, by id, comment id or hashid (a comment resolves to its thread, with `focus_message_id`). The header alone by default; `full`, `brief` (from the latest summary_until on) or `digest` (the snapshots) for the thread. `actionable`, `claimable`, `unread` and the votes are the caller's.

methods.name: ticket.import
methods.description: Upstream coupling — manual import: fetch an external issue (`gh#123`, which needs a default binding, or `gh:owner/repo#123`) and file a ticket coupled to it. Nothing here runs by itself.

methods.name: ticket.list
methods.description: The ticket list an agent works from (`ticket_list`): its filters are the query the route took (`project`, `open`, `actionable`, `claimable`, `tag`, `since`…), each a string or a yes/no.

methods.name: ticket.mark_read
methods.description: Mark a ticket's events read for the caller, up to `up_to_id` when given (#B.191).

methods.name: ticket.mark_unread
methods.description: Mark a ticket unread again for the caller; the answer carries its row.

methods.name: ticket.move
methods.description: Move a ticket, whole thread, to another project : its reporter or a human. The answer is the moved head , with the canonical row.

methods.name: ticket.payload
methods.description: A ticket's payload, filtered: every key, values only where the schema says. No secret in it.

methods.name: ticket.pending_children
methods.description: A ticket's pending `child_of` children, one level, with who attached each and when.

methods.name: ticket.postpone
methods.description: Snooze a ticket (#B.329) until `until` (ISO 8601): hidden from the open inbox until then, when the reveal job brings it back. a human's gesture only: an agent never deals with snooze.

methods.name: ticket.relate
methods.description: Relate two tickets (#B.123 / #275): child_of / parent_of (a lineage, kept a tree), depends_on / blocks, related. A human, the reporter of either ticket, a project-owner of either project, or for depends_on / blocks the agent either is assigned to. The same relation twice is a no-op.

methods.name: ticket.release
methods.description: #418 / #436: release what the caller holds, back to the shared pool: an agent its own claim; the assignee or a moderator the assignment.

methods.name: ticket.revoke_payload
methods.description: Revoke: the values are destroyed, the trace that they existed stays.

methods.name: ticket.set_milestone
methods.description: Put a ticket in a milestone, move it to another, or take it out (`milestone_id: null`). Planning: a human's gesture or a cto agent's.

methods.name: ticket.set_owner
methods.description: #352: change a ticket's owner (its reporter). The new owner is subscribed, so they get the thread's pings; owner-bypass (close/reopen) follows it. the new owner is `owner`; `by_agent` is the author, the caller.

methods.name: ticket.set_payload
methods.description: Deposit or replace a ticket's payload; `schema` names the keys that are public.

methods.name: ticket.step
methods.description: Tag the ticket's latest comment, an agent's, as a step.

methods.name: ticket.subscribe
methods.description: Follow a ticket, or mute it (`muted`: no pings, even by role).

methods.name: ticket.subscribers
methods.description: A ticket's explicit subscriptions, follows and mutes, for the moderator who manages who else is pinged (owners pinged by their role are not listed).

methods.name: ticket.subscription
methods.description: A consumer's relation to one ticket: "followed", "muted", or null (its role decides).

methods.name: ticket.subscriptions
methods.description: The tickets a consumer follows or muted, beyond its projects' roles.

methods.name: ticket.unsnooze
methods.description: Bring a snoozed ticket back now.

methods.name: ticket.unstep
methods.description: Remove that step tag.

methods.name: ticket.unsubscribe
methods.description: Stop following (or unmute) a ticket: back to what the consumer's role says.

methods.name: token_usage.timeseries
methods.description: Token usage over time, per project. Takes a snapshot first when the throttle allows, so the series fills even without a boot job.

methods.name: unread.count
methods.description: How many unread events the consumer has, in one project or all.

methods.name: unread.list
methods.description: The consumer's unread events, oldest first (#800: across projects when `project` is left out), each stamped with whether a human wrote it and whether its ticket still awaits moderation .

methods.name: unread.mark_read
methods.description: Mark read: one event (`message_id`), a project up to an id (`up_to_id`), a whole project (`all`), or every project (`all_projects`, #1185). Another consumer's backlog, or `delete` (drop instead of mark), is a human moderator's gesture (local socket or the web UI).

methods.name: upload.max_bytes
methods.description: How large one upload may be.

methods.name: upload.set_max_bytes
methods.description: Change how large one upload may be (up to the hard cap).

refusal.message: a method's refusal: the JSON-RPC code is the HTTP status it matches, data.code is aiball's error code
